sanskrit: indraṃ vayaṃ vaṇijo havāmahe sa nas trātā pura etu prajānan | ghnann arātiṃ paripanthinaṃ mṛgaṃ sa īśāno dhanadā astu mahyam ||
english: We merchants call upon Indra; may he come before us as our knowing protector. Slaying the grudging foe who lurks along the path like a beast, may he who is sovereign be the giver of wealth to me.

sanskrit: paṇo no astu prapaṇo vikrayaś ca pratipaṇo no dhaninaḥ kṛṇotu | saṃrarāṇā āhutiṃ juṣantāṃ śunaṃ no astu caritam utthitaṃ ca ||
english: May our trading thrive, our selling, and our resale; may the counter-trade make us wealthy. May the gods, rejoicing together, accept the oblation; may our going forth and our return be auspicious.

sanskrit: yat paṇena pratipaṇaṃ carāmi svena devā dhanam icchamānaḥ | indro me tasmin rucam ā dadhātu bṛhaspatiḥ savitā somo agniḥ ||
english: When I go about trading and counter-trading, seeking wealth through my own means, O gods — may Indra, Bṛhaspati, Savitā, Soma, and Agni place brilliance in that enterprise for me.

sanskrit: ye vaḥ panthā bahavo devayānā anu dyāvāpṛthivī saṃcaranti | teṣām ahaṃ māṃ varcasyā dadhāmi yathā krītvā dhanam ā vahāni ||
english: The many god-traveled paths of yours that pass along heaven and earth — upon those I place myself in radiance, so that having purchased goods I may carry wealth home.

sanskrit: viddhavāsase nirṛter ye ca pāśā apaśritāḥ | tebhyaḥ pra mucyate varmī viṣkandham upa sādayan ||
english: The nooses of Nirṛti that have been fastened to the tattered garment — from those the one who wears armor is freed, as he approaches, laying the joint-evil to rest.

sanskrit: na vai tad vāso bhavati yasmin vidhyanti pūruṣam | asnā samajyate rūpaṃ tasmāt tad apalopyam ||
english: That is truly no garment in which they pierce a man; the form is smeared together with blood. Therefore that must be stripped off.

sanskrit: uttiṣṭhann apriyāyata- -avidvān bahubhājyam | na panthāṃ bhadram aśnute ya enena carāt saha ||
english: Rising up, the unknowing one became disliked, one who was to share in much. He does not attain a good path, he who travels along with that one.

sanskrit: brahmaṇaitat pratigṛhyaṃ tena tat kṛṇute śivam | ārkāt pramucyate pāśāt tena dātā vi paśyati ||
english: This, to be received by a brahmin — through it he makes that auspicious. Through it the giver is freed from the noose of the arka plant and sees clearly.

sanskrit: yau vyāghrāv avarūḍhāv avāñcau jighatsataḥ pitaraṃ mātaraṃ ca | tau dantau brahmaṇā brahmaṇaspate śivau kṛṇu tvam iha jātavedaḥ ||
english: Those two teeth, like two descended tigers pointing downward, that seek to devour both the father and the mother — those two teeth, O Bṛhaspati, O Jātavedas, make auspicious here through the sacred word.

sanskrit: vrīhim attaṃ yavam attaṃ māṣam attam atho tilam | sa vāṃ bhāgo nihito ratnadheyaṃ mā hiṃsiṣṭaṃ pitaraṃ mātaraṃ ca ||
english: Eat the rice, eat the barley, eat the black beans, and also the sesame. That is your portion laid out as the holding of a jewel — harm not the father and the mother.

sanskrit: aghorau sayujā saṃvidānau syonau dantau sumaṅgalau | mā hiṃsiṣṭaṃ pitaraṃ mātaraṃ ca- -anyatra vāṃ tanvo ghoram astu ||
english: Non-fierce, yoked together, in agreement, gentle — be these teeth of good omen. Harm not the father and the mother; let what is terrible in your nature be elsewhere.

sanskrit: enā yutām indrāgnī rājñā somena medinā | indro marutvān ādānam amitrebhyaḥ kṛṇotu me ||
english: By this let Indra and Agni be yoked, together with King Soma the ally. May Indra, attended by the Maruts, make the seizure against my enemies for me.

sanskrit: idam ādānam akaraṃ tapasendreṇa saṃśitam | amitrā yatra santi me tān ādāṃ dviṣato mama ||
english: I have performed this seizure, sharpened by Indra through austerity. Wherever my enemies are, those who hate me — I seize them.

sanskrit: ādānena saṃdānena- -amitrān saṃ dyāmasi | apānā ye caiṣāṃ prāṇā asunāsūn sam acchidam ||
english: With seizing and with binding we crush the enemies. Their out-breaths and their in-breaths — their vital forces one by one I have cut off.

sanskrit: pratūrtāya marutvate svāhā ||
english: Svāhā to the swift-rushing one, the one accompanied by Maruts!

sanskrit: jayadvīrāyābhiṣatvane svāhā ||
english: Svāhā to the victory-hero, the one who overwhelms his foes!

sanskrit: bṛhaspataye viśvadevāvate svāhā ||
english: Svāhā to Bṛhaspati, who has all the gods with him!

sanskrit: pra dyauḥ pra pṛthivī prāntarikṣaṃ svam arhat | pretaḥ samudriyā āpaḥ śalyam acucyavuḥ ||
english: Heaven stirs forth, earth stirs forth, the mid-space stirs forth, each into its own realm. Forward — the oceanic waters have shaken the thorn loose.

sanskrit: pra tvā vātaś cyāvayatu pra bhūmiḥ sahasā saha | pretaḥ samudriyā āpaḥ śalyam acucyavuḥ ||
english: May the wind shake you forth, may the earth with its might. Forward — the oceanic waters have shaken the thorn loose.

sanskrit: pra tvā sūryaś cyāvayatu nakṣatraiḥ saha medibhiḥ | pretaḥ samudriyā āpaḥ śalyam acucyavuḥ ||
english: May the sun shake you forth, together with the nourishing lunar mansions. Forward — the oceanic waters have shaken the thorn loose.

sanskrit: yo mā pautudruvo maṇir viśvabheṣaja āgamat | so asmat sarvaṃ duṣvapnyam apa hantu tamaś ca yat ||
english: The amulet pautudruva that has come to me, the universal medicine — may it strike away from us all evil dreaming and whatever darkness there is.

sanskrit: apāsmat sarvaṃ duṣvapnyam apa pāpīṃ ca lakṣmyam | adhā hiraṇyavarcasaṃ sarvadā mā maṇe kṛdhi ||
english: Away from us all evil dreaming, and away the evil omen. Now, O amulet, make me always golden-splendored.

sanskrit: sarvadaivāhaṃ bhagavān indriyāvān viṣāsahiḥ | yo mā pautudruvo maṇir draviṇena sahāruhad indreṇa sahāruhat ||
english: Always let me be one possessed of fortune, full of vigor, capable of enduring all. The pautudruva amulet that has mounted me together with wealth, has mounted together with Indra.

sanskrit: pumān aśvo dhanaṃ vittiṃ pumān niṣko hiraṇyayaḥ | pumāṃsaṃ putram oṣadhe 'syā ā dhehi nāryai ||
english: A male horse, wealth, property; a male golden ornament — O herb, place a male son in this woman.

sanskrit: yathānandāḥ puṃsi jāte na vravastīti kaś cana | evā tvaṃ putram oṣadhe 'syā ā dhehi nāryai ||
english: Just as when a male is born there is rejoicing and no one says a word against it — in just that way, O herb, place a son in this woman.

sanskrit: aśvena riṣyena gavā krītāsy oṣadhe | aśvaḥ śveto dhanaṃ tava hiraṇyaṃ haritaṃ tava | dattā somena rājñeha puṃsavanaṃ bhava ||
english: You, O herb, are purchased with a horse, with an antelope, with a cow. A white horse is your wealth, gold and greenery are yours. Given by King Soma, be here an agent of male offspring.

sanskrit: yan me nṛmṇaṃ draviṇaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ ca yac ca śrutaṃ yac ca ratnaṃ bibharmi | etan no atra nidhipānu pātu yāvad aimi strīyaṇamajmā vyajya ||
english: Whatever manly strength, wealth, sacred lore, and whatever learning and jewel I bear — may the guardian of the deposit protect this here for us while I go traversing the womens' way beyond.

sanskrit: yan me nṛmṇaṃ draviṇaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ ca ye agnayo dhṛṣṇiyāso mayīme | hariścandro rakṣatu tan no atra yāvad aimi paro grāmaṃ caritvā ||
english: Whatever manly strength, wealth, sacred knowledge, and whatever bold fires belong to me — may Hariścandra protect that here for us while I go beyond, having traveled through the village.

sanskrit: eṣa aimi paro grāmaṃ caritvā- -accha nṛmṇaṃ draviṇaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ ca | yad atrāpi tve śuci- -idaṃ tad aham ā dade ||
english: Here I go, having traveled beyond the village, toward manly strength, wealth, and sacred lore. Whatever is pure here in you — this I take to myself.

sanskrit: ā sūryo hi prathamaṃ dasyuhatyāya śakra hārī yuñjāno maghavan sahasram | dāsaṃ varṇaṃ randhayann āryāya yuñjāno bāhū puruhūta vajram ||
english: For indeed the Sun yoked first the thousand dappled ones for slaying the dasyu, O powerful and bounteous one; subduing the dāsa color for the Ārya, yoking the two arms and the vajra, O much-invoked one.

sanskrit: āhṛḍate dasyuhatyāya tūrṇa dṛḍhāni parvā śṛṇīhīndra | tīvrāśraddho bahulāny eṣām ayujvano arpaya saṃ vadhena ||
english: Come swiftly for the slaying of the dasyu; O Indra, shatter their strong joints. Being fierce of purpose and faith, those who are unyoked — smash many of them together with the stroke.

sanskrit: darśan nu citrapāvānam indraṃ bahu sākaṃ śarām̐ iva patyamānān | ye no ghṛṣviṃ maghavānaṃ pṛtanyān abhīru teṣu kavayo vavṛtyuḥ ||
english: For now they have seen Indra, of bright purifying might, many falling together like arrows. Those who battle against our bold and bounteous one — fearlessly the wise ones have turned against them.

sanskrit: idāvatsarāya parivatsarāya saṃvatsarāya prati vedayāma etat | yad vrateṣu duritaṃ nijagmima durhārdaṃ tena śamalenāñjmaḥ ||
english: To the current year, to the passing year, to the full year — we make known this. Whatever wrongdoing we have fallen into in our vows, by that fault of evil-heartedness we have become besmirched.

sanskrit: yan me vrataṃ vratapate lulobha- -ahorātre sam adhātāṃ ma etat | udyan purastād bhiṣag astu candramāḥ sūryo raśmibhir abhi gṛṇātv etat ||
english: O lord of vows, whatever vow of mine has gone astray — may day and night together settle this for me. May the moon, rising in the east, be the healer; may the sun with his rays approve this.

sanskrit: yad vratam atipede cittyā manasā hṛdā | ādityā rudrās tan mayi vasavaś ca sam indhatām ||
english: Whatever vow I have transgressed by thought, by mind, by heart — may the Ādityas, the Rudras, and the Vasus kindle that aright in me.

sanskrit: vratāni vratapataya upā karomy agnaye | sa me dyumnaṃ bṛhad yaśo dīrgham āyuṣ kṛṇotu me ||
english: I bring the vows to Agni, the lord of vows. May he make for me great brilliance, vast fame, and long life.

sanskrit: mayobhūr vāto abhi vātūsrā ūrjasvatīr oṣadhīr ā riśantām | medasvatīr jīvadhanyā mayobhuvaḥ padvate 'vasāya rudra mṛḍa ||
english: May the well-being-bringing wind blow upon us; may the radiant, vigor-bearing herbs come nigh. O Rudra, grant bliss to the footed creature — the fat-filled, life-giving, well-being-bringing ones — for his refuge.

sanskrit: yā ekarūpā viśvarūpāḥ sarūpā yāsām agnir ūdho vo janma veda | yā aṅgirasas tapaseha cakrus tābhyaḥ parjanya mahi śarma yacchāt ||
english: Those cows of one form, of all forms, of equal form — those whose birth and udder Agni knows — those that the Aṅgirasas made here for austerity: to them may Parjanya extend great shelter.

sanskrit: yā deveṣu tanva airayanta yāsāṃ somo rūpadheyāni veda | tā asmabhyaṃ bahulāḥ pinvamānāḥ prajāvatīr indra goṣṭhe didiśyāḥ ||
english: Those cows that have spread their bodies among the gods, whose forms and names Soma knows — may those, swelling in numbers, rich in offspring, be pointed out for us, O Indra, in the cowpen.

sanskrit: prajāpatir mahyam etā rarāṇo bahvīḥ satīr upa me goṣṭha ākaḥ | tāsāṃ vayaṃ prajayā saṃ sadema jyog jīvantaḥ śaradaḥ purūcīḥ ||
english: Prajāpati, delighting in me, has driven many true ones here into my cowpen. May we dwell together with their offspring, living long through many autumns.

sanskrit: abhiṣṭhitā carkardīti piśaṅgī bahukardinī | kardo ha jajñe hālīkṣṇād vrīher māṣād atho yavāt ||
english: Mounted and churning about is the tawny one, the much-churner. The grain-smut was born from the straw-chaff, from rice, from black beans, and also from barley.

sanskrit: yathā bhasad dhālīkṣṇasya na saṃbhavati kardave | evā halagna kardaya nir grāmān nir diśo jahi ||
english: Just as the rump of the straw-chaff does not come together in the grain-smut — in just that way, O plow-attendant, drive the grain-smut out from the villages, drive it out to the directions.

sanskrit: yathā parasvāṃ chardhate gardabhaḥ kṛdhusandṛśaḥ | evā te śardhatāṃ bhasad dhālīkṣṇaparṇa śardhaya vṛtrahā śākī śardhaya ||
english: Just as a donkey, of contracted appearance, breaks wind at its neighbor — in just that way let your rump fart, O straw-chaff leaf; O Vṛtra-slayer, O Śāki, make it fart.

sanskrit: pavīraval lāṅgalaṃ suśevaṃ somapitsaram | tad ut kṛṣati gām aviṃ prapharvyaṃ ca pīvarīṃ prastāvaṃ rathavāhanam ||
english: Pointed like a spike, pleasant, thirsty for Soma — the plow draws up the fat cow, the ewe, the spirited mare, and the draft animal of the chariot.

sanskrit: śunaṃ varatrām ā yaccha śunam aṣṭrām ud iṅgaya | śunaṃ vāhasya yuktasya- -aṣṭrayā jahi dakṣiṇam ||
english: Draw taut the harness for good fortune; brandish the goad for good fortune. Strike the right side of the yoked draft animal with the goad for good fortune.

sanskrit: madhumantaṃ ni gṛhāṇa phālaṃ kṣetreṣu sarvadā | tat parjanyo 'bhi varṣatu bhūmne dhānyāya kartave ||
english: Hold down the honey-sweet plowshare in the fields at all times; may Parjanya rain upon it for abundance, to make the grain.

sanskrit: etā u tyā adṛkṣata- -āyatīr vedyām adhi | prāhāgnir havyaṃ devebhyo mantro hotā haviṣpatiḥ ||
english: These very ones were seen coming toward the vedi. Agni sent forward the offering to the gods; the sacred formula is the hotr, the lord of oblations.

sanskrit: emā agur mayobhuvo madhor ūdhāṃsi bibhratīḥ | tā upa pra śikṣata duhānā akṣitaṃ payaḥ ||
english: These well-being-bringing ones have come, bearing udders full of sweetness. Learn from those that are milking inexhaustible milk.

sanskrit: iḍā stha madhupṛco viśvarūpās tā mā viśata | saha prāṇena tejasā harasā balena ||
english: You are the iḍā offerings, honey-mixed, of all forms — enter me, together with breath, with radiance, with ardor, with strength.
